inspiration: RE-friction duplicate needs on CryptoME.exe: an existing flow 0x4f700b branch assertion restores the proven stack-built transfer without defining encrypted target bytes
decisions: Reuse entryretdispatch's bounded raw-p-code affine stack provenance instead of adding an instruction-text matcher or a second flow engine.
Accept only the one-store form whose RETURN loads that exact current-run slot, whose store value is constant, and whose RET advances the same stack base by the loaded width.
Decline any second live same-stack store, leaving push continuation; push target; ret exclusively under entryretdispatch's call-emulation classifier.
Seed BRANCH, never CALL: the original function has no fall-through after push immediate; ret. The C printer may spell the terminal branch as an indirect tail-call statement.
Caller-supplied flow facts own their sites. Explicit RETURN is a clean veto and is not redundantly applied to an already-RETURN instruction.
Never create a function at the constant destination because the CryptoME target bytes are ciphertext until the unpacker runs.
Replace both weak dataset acceptances with one vendored PE acceptance matching the full unpacker-call plus switch/case control-flow sequence inside JSON code, so warning text alone cannot pass.
Ship default on because the default-on ablation changes 0 of 675 assertions and the exact CryptoME entry is within the 5% speed-regression budget.

controls.target_discovery: function inventory remains without the encrypted 0x401000 PE destination before and after decompilation
